Everything below is measured [M] unless labelled otherwise. The work took about 3 h 15 min, over the 2.5 h time box.

io_gt.py works.
- All seven refusals pass: an align path, scan, loc, parquet, MOCAP, the key 'pose', and a symlink to an align file.
- Poses load (ep2: 343 frames). The download path returns identical arrays.

refine.py design:
- Per-frame normals come from the same frame, oriented to its camera.
- The consensus is side-keyed 3 mm surfels, each moved to the frame-balanced weighted median of its 6 mm neighbourhood.
- Each frame is aligned by trimmed, Cauchy-weighted point-to-plane ICP with a weak prior (2 deg / 5 mm) and hard bounds (3 deg / 10 mm).
- The mean correction is removed after every pass (gauge), over 3 passes with gates of 12, 8 and 6 mm.
- v2 (the default, added after the pre-registered run) skips updates along Hessian directions that hold less than 1.5 % of the largest information (Zhang, Kaess and Singh 2016, "solution remapping").

Injection-recovery on lid ep2 (real points, known AR(1) per-frame errors of about 1 deg / 1.5 mm sd per component):
- Correlation between applied and recovered errors is 0.91-0.98 for rotation and 0.98-0.995 for translation.
- The error sd is 0.23-0.35 deg and 0.17-0.26 mm.
- The residual after refinement is 0.480 mm, against 0.474 mm when nothing was injected.
- So the estimator does recover rigid per-frame errors.

Pre-registered falsifier: FAIL. Format is between / within in mm, and pass means between < within.
- v1, ep41:
  - 140-180 mm band: 9.34 → 4.70 / 3.65, FAIL.
  - 180-220 mm band: 5.58 → 3.03 / 4.13, pass.
  - 220-250 mm band: 6.23 → 3.69 / 5.34, pass.
- v1, ep42:
  - 140-180 mm band: 7.46 → 6.09 / 5.11, FAIL.
  - 180-220 mm band: 6.67 → 4.02 / 6.86, pass.
  - 220-250 mm band: 26.9 → 22.14 / 6.07, FAIL. This band was flagged as contaminated before the run: its median offset is +14 mm.
- v2 gives the same verdict: ep41 140-180 is 4.68 / 3.64 and ep42 140-180 is 5.71 / 5.21.
- Refinement roughly halves the handle spread, but does not bring it below the within-frame width in every band.
- Confound ruled out: every frame saw the handle from the same side in both episodes, so seeing two faces does not explain the spread.

Held-out controls, all post-hoc and not part of the falsifier:
- Handle wedge excluded from the fit:
  - The handle gets worse: ep41 140-250 mm bands 13.9 / 14.6 / 16.1 mm (v1) and 13.9 / 14.1 / 16.3 (v2); ep42 is also worse.
  - In v1 the rotation about the pot axis wanders (sd 2.0 deg, against 0.65 deg in the full run). v2 freezes that direction, yet the handle is still at 14 mm.
  - decomp_check shows why. Tilt and translation are strongly coupled: in the full run each alone smears the handle to 9-11 mm and only together do they sharpen it. Without the handle the body cannot set that combination.
  - The per-frame smallest Hessian eigenvalue drops from 0.02-0.035 to 0.005-0.008 of the largest.
- Outer handle (r ≥ 180 mm) held out, with the inner handle used in the fit:
  - ep42 outer 180-220 band: 6.67 → 3.93, transfers like the full run (4.02).
  - ep41 outer bands get WORSE than raw: 7.46 (raw 5.58) and 8.30 (raw 6.23).
- Mixed evidence: in ep41 the handle's own points are needed to sharpen it, so the full-run sharpening cannot be told apart from self-fitting. The jitter hypothesis is neither confirmed nor cleanly refuted.

Generic statistics, from 33 refined files (32 with frames fitted; all_summary.json):
- Median per-frame residual to the consensus: 0.749 → 0.588 mm. It does not drop for pot ep41 (0.72 → 0.75) or ep42 (0.77 → 0.77).
- Patch between-frame spread (5 mm patches) falls by a median 22 % (10-49 %) in every file.
- After refinement it is still 4.1× the within-frame width (5.7× before), and in 93-100 % of patches between exceeds within. Most of the frame-to-frame scatter is not removed by rigid per-frame correction [H: non-rigid stereo depth error].
- Corrections: median per-file p50 is 1.39 deg and 2.32 mm.
- 600 of 3802 fitted frames hit a bound. Bound hits are high for mini_sweeper (72/177, 56/144) and mini_dust_pan (69/160, 44/130).
- Corrections are temporally correlated: lag-1 autocorrelation is mostly 0.3-0.8.
- ep0 lid: all 24 frames skipped (too few points), so its refined copy equals the raw file.

Marker-ball radius from public observations only:
- ball_scan (residual clusters above a robust quadric, free sphere fit, generic acceptance tests) accepted 11 detections in 9 of 33 files.
- Median 9.7 mm, IQR 8.4-10.2, MAD 1.05, range 7.2-12.8.
- Only one ball was found again in a second episode (pot, 12.8 and 10.3 mm).
- On lid ep2 the radius depends on the method: 9.4-10.6 mm at a 2.5 mm protrusion threshold, and no usable cap at 4 mm. Stereo spreads a ball over a band about 4 mm thick in radius.
- My verdict: this does not reliably replace the 7 mm prior. Treat the radius as about 7-10 mm, uncertain [H: the stereo fits are biased upward].

builds.module: autokit/shell.py: route A, the generic thin-shell mesh engine. It works from one episode's observed points with no part vocabulary. The points become oriented surface samples through a point-based directional TSDF, and the samples become a closed thin solid by marching cubes.
api: thin_shell(obs: dict, t=0.0025, voxel=0.002, mode='oriented', two_sided=True, carve=False, max_faces=200000, pitch=None, return_report=False, **kw) -> trimesh.Trimesh (watertight). With return_report=True it returns (mesh, report dict). The report is also stored in mesh.metadata['shell_report']. obs needs pts and cam; frame is optional.

mode='oriented' (default): the solid lies behind the observed face, on the side away from the cameras, so the observed face stays in place. mode='symmetric': a tube of +-t/2 around the surface, the unsigned-distance variant from the task.

two_sided=True: where both faces of a wall were observed (searched up to 10 mm along -n), the measured thickness replaces t. Measured thickness is floored at T_FLOOR = 1.5 mm, the smallest value on the generic grid.
carve=True (oriented mode, default off): our own rays, moved onto the denoised surface, cut each slab back where at least 3 frames saw free space behind the surface.
Marching-cubes pitch = min(voxel, 0.95*min(t, min tau)/sqrt(3)), so no slab can fall between grid points.

Lower-level functions: point_normals(P,C,F,vox), directional_samples(P,n,vox) -> dict(s,n,w,bin), two_sided_thickness(S,N), free_space_clamp(P,C,F,n,S,N,tau,depth_max), shell_field(S,N,tau,offset,rdisk,pitch), march(U,lo,pitch), clean_islands(m,P,F), decimate(m,max_faces).

All numbers here were measured on this VM [M] unless marked otherwise.

What was built: a generic route that needs no part vocabulary and works from one episode. It has six steps.
1. Normals per frame. One depth map sees one side of a wall as a single layer, so per-frame normals are sharp. Points with a non-planar neighbourhood or seen at more than 78 degrees incidence are dropped.
2. Directional fusion. Centroids are keyed by voxel and by the normal's dominant signed axis. Each centroid is then projected onto its own side's mean surface: a weighted mean offset along its normal line, inside a 5 mm truncation band, using only neighbours whose normal is within 45 degrees of its own. This is the TSDF zero crossing, without the edges of bins.
3. Two-sided thickness, where both faces of a wall were seen.
4. A union of disc slabs. Default 'oriented' mode keeps the observed face in place and puts thickness t behind it, away from the cameras.
5. Marching cubes in a narrow band (Lewiner). The output is closed by construction.
6. Island filter (frame support, area, distance to the main body), then quadric decimation to 200k faces.

Synthetic tube (truth: faces at 34 and 40 mm):
- Oriented with two-sided thickness gives exactly two faces, at 33.75 and 39.75 mm (0.25 mm histogram bins). The outer face has p10/p50/p90 = 39.93/39.97/40.02 mm at every azimuth. Measured wall thickness p10/p50/p90 = 5.94/6.01/6.08 mm (truth 6.0). One body, watertight.
- Without two-sided thickness: faces at 33.75, about 37 (two back faces) and 39.75 mm, as expected.
- Symmetric mode: faces at 32.75, 35.25, 38.75 and 41.25 mm, so the observed face moves by t/2, as expected.
- Two earlier designs failed here. Pooled-cloud PCA normals plus a 3-D Gaussian window left the faces stuck 1-2 mm off. Overlapping 60-degree bins bulged the outer face by up to 1 mm at the bin edges. Both were replaced.

builds.module: autokit/gates.py: GT-free selector v2. Gates measure each (mesh, episode) pair and select() picks with a frozen rank; library_v3 is the fallback.
api: evaluate(mesh_path, obs_paths: list, obj: str, ep: int, flip=True) -> dict(mesh, obj, ep, obs, metrics, gates, pass, rank_score, per_frame, thresholds, sec). obs_paths: io_gt files. A refined copy is detected by its sibling .corr.npz; its per-frame correction is composed into cam_T_obj (cam_T_obj[f] @ inv([R | c0 + t - R c0])).

select(rows: list) -> dict(pick, reasons, ranking). Takes the rows of one object. library_v3 rows (or rows with fallback=True) are always eligible and never gated. Other rows must pass every gate on every episode they were evaluated on. Rank = mean rank_score; ties go to the lower fid_sum_mm.
rank_score(m) = dr_cdist_mm + dr_pdist_mm, lower is better. This is a two-sided truncated depth residual along camera rays, judged only where the object was observed. CAP = 12 mm.
gates_of(m) -> {G_COMP, G_HOLE, G_PREC, G_FS, G_CONN, G_TOPO, G_FRAME, G_FLIP}. A missing or NaN measure fails its gate.

**Candidate tables**

*white_pot_lid ep2* (no hold-out; ep0 is excluded as the known bad track). All 11 candidates pass every gate.
- shell_raw t1.5 / 2.5 / 4.0: rank 0.228 / 0.248 / 0.344 [0.257 / 0.271 / 0.377]. comp 1.000, hole3d 0.000, viol 0.006-0.012, fs 0.026-0.070, conn 0.98-0.99.

*blue_cup ep21 + ep22*
- shell_raw_t1.5: passes both episodes; rank 0.664 / 0.676 [0.551]; viol 0.023.
- shell_raw_t2.5: passes both; 0.780 / 0.696.

- dsl_lathe_splat and its +union variant, at every t: fail G_PREC on both episodes (viol 0.079 / 0.064); rank 1.759 / 1.404.
- incumbent lathe_obs_g1: same result; 1.759 / 1.409.

*mini_dust_pan ep39 + ep18, ep40*
- shell_raw_t1.5: passes own (rank 0.474). Fails G_HOLE on ep18 (0.097, rank 0.967) and on ep40 (0.075, plus G_FS, rank 1.323).
- shell_raw_t2.5: own 0.585; G_HOLE on both hold-outs (0.091 / 0.069).

- shell_ref t1.5-4.0: G_FS everywhere (0.19-0.28), plus G_HOLE on the hold-outs.

*water_pitcher ep22 + ep21*
- shell_raw_t1.5: passes own (1.156); fails G_HOLE on ep21 (0.078, rank 1.580).
- shell_raw_t2.5: own 1.341; G_HOLE on ep21 (0.051).

*mini_sweeper ep31 + ep18*
- Every shell fails G_CONN (0.944-0.956) on all episodes; own ranks 0.285-0.617.
- On ep18 every candidate, the library included, fails G_COMP (0.69-0.71) and G_HOLE (0.26-0.29).
- library_v3 passes own (0.897).
- Post hoc, the +main variants pass G_CONN (1.0). shell_raw_t1.5+main ranks 0.334, but its hole3d rises from 0.002 to 0.020 because the dropped 13.7 cm² island was observed surface.

**What broke: interface and policy mismatches**

No other module was edited.
1. **Flip check run once per mesh.** gates.evaluate takes an extra `flip` argument. Because flip_check compares the mesh with library_v3 and does not depend on the episode, run_object runs it once per mesh and copies it into the hold-out and raw-obs rows, re-running gates.gates_of. This saves about 20-35 s per extra row. Across two runs, all 21 shared sweeper rows came out identical [M].
2. **Library mesh referenced in place.** gates.select keys rows by mesh path and recognises the fallback by its directory. So library_v3 must be referenced where it lies, never copied. run_object maps paths back to candidate names.
3. **Stale vote grids in refined copies.** refine.py copies the raw vote grids unchanged (grids_stale). On refined observations, fs_frac therefore compares refined-built meshes against raw grids. Not fixed; reported.
4. **Shell island rule vs G_CONN.** shell.clean_islands keeps islands within 30 mm of the body that enough frames saw; G_CONN counts only components that touch (2 mm) plus compact balls. Every sweeper shell fails G_CONN as a result. The post-hoc main_group variant lives in the integration layer and uses the gates' own constants; it passes G_CONN but drops observed surface.
5. **Gates miss what budget_mesh does to shells.** G_TOPO and G_CONN are measured on the mesh as built, so neither sees what budget_mesh does to the shell picks:

   | Shell pick | Bodies before → after | Area before → after (cm²) | Change | Watertight after |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | Lid | 6 → 32 | 644 → 622 | −3 % | yes |
   | Cup | 2 → 47 | 665 → 639 | −4 % | no |
   | Dust pan | 3 → 74 | 575 → 524 | −9 % | no |
   | Pitcher | 24 → 165 | 2126 → 1685 | −21 % | no |

   Only the depth-render terms use the decoded mesh.
6. **lathe_splat ignores t.** Its output is identical at t 1.5, 2.5 and 4.0: the two-sided measured wall of 1.96 mm replaces t. That gives 3 duplicate candidates per variant, so the t-grid robustness test is vacuous for this program.
7. **Shell metadata dropped before export.** The thin_shell report in mesh.metadata is popped before GLB export, as a precaution; the report is saved to the build json instead.
8. **Very large pitcher shells.** The pitcher shell at t 1.5 keeps 0.93-1.10 M faces, because decimation to 200k is rejected when the result is not watertight. Its evaluation is slower (about 50 s on its own episode).
9. **Leaked lid meshes excluded.** The lid hand-kit fit_v* meshes used scan thicknesses, so they are not candidates; the clean-round t2.5 mesh is used instead.

**Main findings**
- **Refined points never help.** Refined shells never beat raw ones: they tie on the lid (0.229 vs 0.228). On the cup, dust pan and pitcher they fail G_PREC or G_FS on the own episode, on raw observations and on the hold-outs. On cup ep21, refine moved frames by a median 5.4 mm (p90 10.0 mm, at the bound) with 36 bound hits. Refined observations should not be a default input [M on 4 objects].
- **Hold-outs expose surface the build episode never saw.** On the dust pan and pitcher, shells pass on their own episode, but the hold-outs show coherent unexplained surface (hole3d 0.05-0.10). Eval-time selection, which sees one episode, would ship those shells. Route A alone is incomplete; closing the unseen surface needs B programs or a completeness prior [M].
- **The fallback gets a free pass.** On the dust pan the library fails G_HOLE worse than the shells (0.11-0.15 vs 0.06-0.10), yet it wins because it is never gated.
- **The sweeper hold-out is contaminated.** ep18 sweeper points lie p90 38.7 mm from library_v3 (ep31: 3.6 mm) and their centroid is shifted 32 mm. Possible cause: the dust pan is in the same scene [H]. Its hold-out verdict is not usable.
- **The rank prefers the thinnest shell.** The shell rank rises monotonically with t on own episodes and on hold-outs, so t1.5 always wins (see the shell builder's caveat).
- **The rank disagrees with one known CD-O ordering.** On the lid it puts library_v3 (0.489) above the clean hand-kit incumbent (0.539). STATUS (07:10, scan round) found the opposite on CD-O. This is context only; no scan number is used by any code.

audits.verdict:
All numbers below are measured here [M] on the CPU VM with the uncommitted working tree (HEAD f81a953). Everything was GT-free: no scan, *_align, mocap or parquet file was opened, and mesh_metric.py was not run. Review scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/auto/stage1/review/.

The modules mostly do what their builders report:
- refine.py reproduces bit-exactly and does not move the object frame.
- The thin shells are deterministic, watertight at full resolution and sit tightly on the observed points.
- The DSL reproduces the hand kits exactly.
- The camera wiring in gates.py is correct.

But the parts do not yet combine into a working A+B engine. One issue blocks it and several are major.

**(1) Refine.**
- The pre-registered falsifier fails again, with identical numbers:
  - ep41, 140-180 mm band: 4.68 vs 3.64 mm.
  - ep42: 5.71 vs 5.21 mm, and the 220-250 mm band at 22.3 mm.
- The frame does not drift:
  - net rigid change 0.06-0.28 deg and at most 0.29 mm;
  - median distance to library_v3 goes from 2.14 to 1.98 mm (ep41) and from 2.364 to 2.368 mm (ep42).
- On near-cylinders refine slides frames along the axis. On the cup in ep21 the axial correction reaches the 10 mm bound. Its patch_spread metric cannot see that sliding.

**(2) Shell.**
- Size relative to the observations is right: at most 0.1 % of the shell area lies more than 5 mm from any observed point.
- It is one main body plus small flakes (conn_share ≥ 0.99). The lid, dust pan and pitcher look like the objects.
- The cup shell is missing about a third of its wall and its bottom.
- After budget_mesh none of the shells stays watertight. Area changes by -1 % (lid) to -10 % (pitcher), and the decoded meshes have 16-57 bodies.

**(3) DSL.** Lid ep2 and cup ep21 reproduce at fidelity ratio 1.0012 / 0.9942, with median distance 0.003 / 0.000 mm.

**(4) Gates.**
- They reject the no-wall negative control for the right reason: G_HOLE 0.122.
- Observed points re-project to integer pixels and the camera centres match to within 1e-4 mm. Reversing the correction drops the integer-pixel share to 2 %.
- The gates are graded: inflating a mesh by 6 mm fails them, while 3 mm moves only the rank.
- Two serious gaps:
  - The rank cannot see surface that was never observed, so the incomplete shells always win. The shell is picked over the library and the hand-kit incumbent for the lid and the cup, and the integration run picks shell t1.5.
  - Extra geometry outside the observed silhouette is invisible: an added fin covering 8 % of the area passes every gate and leaves the rank unchanged.

**(5) Authoring from DSL.md alone.** I wrote two dust-pan programs from DSL.md alone. Neither produced a recognisable object:
- plate_set merges connected sheets into one plate.
- Occupancy outlines fill holes, so the ring handle becomes a solid disc.
- Most window parameters are undocumented, and unknown parameters are silently ignored.

So the engine can rebuild known objects but cannot yet make a new one.

- refine's own pre-registered falsifier fails. I reproduced it bit-exactly: stored and re-run refined points differ by 0.0 mm. ep41 140-180 mm band: 4.68 vs 3.64; ep42: 5.71 vs 5.21, and the 220-250 band at 22.33 vs 6.10.
- refine degrades cups (previous finding).
With a curvature-corrected measure (robust quadric residual, review/refine_check.py), 5 of 6 handle bands still fail after refinement:
- ep41: 3.77/2.02, 3.57/2.03, 3.67/4.98;
- ep42: 6.43/2.69, 4.67/1.51, 16.26/9.31.
The frame itself is fine:
- net rigid change 0.06-0.28 deg and at most 0.29 mm;
- distance to library_v3: ep41 2.14 → 1.98 mm, ep42 2.364 → 2.368 mm.
findings.fix:
- Make raw observations the default in gates.evaluate and run_object until the refined copies pass a pre-registered GT-free refined-vs-raw test.
- Re-check the v2 levels on raw observations. LAT_PREC = 6 mm has already been run on raw points in diag_lat.jsonl, so this is cheap.
- Report refined results only as an alternative.

findings.issue:
[M] Closed thin shells do not survive the kit's budget_mesh. G_TOPO cannot catch this, because it checks only watertightness as built plus the decoded face count, so every shell passes it. After the decode:

| Object | Area (cm²) | Change | Bodies |
|---|---|---|---|
| lid ep2 | 657 → 650 | -1.1 % | 28 |
| dust pan ep39 | 572 → 539 | -5.8 % | 27 |
| cup ep22 | 621 → 609 | -2.0 % | 16 |
| pitcher ep22 | 1951 → 1755 | -10.1 % | 57 |

None is watertight.

A grep of the kit's CD-O.py and AUC.py finds no watertight or volume requirement: the scorer only samples the surface by area. A closed shell therefore spends about half of the 4096 faces on a back face that lies within t of the front face.
findings.fix:
- Have shell.py emit at most 4096 faces itself, so that budget_mesh only welds the mesh.
  - Decimate the open, denoised surface to about 4000 faces with a decimator that preserves boundaries.
  - Then either ship it open, or offset it and stitch the rim within budget.
- Gate the decoded mesh: |area_budget/area_raw - 1| ≤ 2 %, RMS-radius change ≤ 1 %, and decoded bodies ≤ raw bodies + balls.

findings.issue:
[M] A stage-2 agent cannot realistically author a program for a new object from DSL.md alone.
- 28 of the 36 window names that parts.py reads through ctx.w are not in DSL.md (e.g. body_w, rim_w, surf_band, dome_r0, hole_grid, t_min, t_max).
- Unknown parameter keys are silently ignored.
- `list(p.get('of', []))` turns a string such as "body" into ['b', 'o', 'd', 'y'], which produces false validation errors.
- The vocabulary has no free-form curved sheet (e.g. the water pitcher), no ring and no swept tube. The only fallback is splat or tsdf_patch.
findings.fix:
- Give each part type a parameter schema (name, default, relative or absolute, meaning) in parts.PART_TYPES. Generate the DSL.md table from it, and make validate_program reject unknown keys.
- Accept a string or a list for 'of'.
- Ship a render-and-compare helper for the authoring loop: crop, point render, and program render.
- Add ring and swept-tube parts before stage 2.

findings.issue: [M, by reading the code] The v2 revisions (refined observations, LAT_PREC 6 mm) were made after v1 rejected three incumbents labelled MUST_PASS. Those labels, and the 'bad' labels on the P2 picks, come from earlier rounds scored against the scans. The thresholds were therefore tuned toward scan-derived outcomes, so the 18-of-19 result is not independent evidence. The builder notes the lack of independence but not this scan-label route.
findings.fix:
- Freeze v2 by sha now.
- Pre-register expected outcomes on objects and episodes not used for tuning (sweeper 18/31, boards 23/24, pitcher 21, pot 43-45), using only synthetic GT-free edits: wall deletion, inflation, fin, shift.
- Do this before stage 2 relies on the gates.

findings.issue:
[M] The falsifier's statistic is confounded.
- One PCA plane is fitted for the whole handle wedge, so the within-frame width includes the handle's own curvature and tilt.
- The per-frame median offset depends on which part of the band each frame sees. Its R² against per-frame coverage is up to 0.92 (ep42 180-220 mm, raw).
- Using a robust quadric residual instead lowers the within-frame widths to 1.5-2.7 mm, and the verdict gets stricter.
findings.fix: Use a per-band robust quadric (or local-surface) residual for both the between and the within statistic, as in review/refine_check.py bands_quadric. Report coverage R² alongside it.
cu = floor((u + 0.5)/CELL_PX), cv = floor((v + 0.5)/CELL_PX). This leaves observed points in the same cells and centres the mesh footprint.

findings.issue:
[M] The island filter keeps flat flakes, not only balls.
- Lid ep2 keeps a 6.3 cm² flake (sphericity 0.53, 3.7 x 28.6 x 29.9 mm, 6.2 mm from the body).
- The pitcher keeps 5 flakes of 1-3.6 cm².
- gates.connectivity classifies only 1 of the 9 secondary bodies as a ball. conn_share is still ≥ 0.99.
findings.fix: Keep a secondary island only if it is ball-like (sphericity ≥ 0.8, diameter ≤ 30 mm) or lies within TOUCH of the main body. Report the dropped area.

findings.issue: [M, from the integ summary] The cup program gives identical meshes at t = 1.5, 2.5 and 4.0 mm (area 983.7 cm² and the same metrics each time), because the wall thickness comes from two-sided evidence. The t-grid robustness check is therefore never exercised. The builder's density test showed this measured t moves from 1.96 to 3.9 mm.
findings.fix: When t_src is two_sided, also build prior-t variants (force t_src = prior) so the grid actually brackets the uncertain thickness.
